reviews.title: Compact and Brilliantly Illuminated
reviews.comment: Let's start with the positives. The compact tenkeyless (TKL) form factor is perfect for gamers who prefer a more streamlined and space-saving setup. It leaves more room for mouse movement and eliminates the need for a dedicated number pad. The build quality is solid, and the keyboard feels durable and well-constructed. The RGB illumination is a standout feature, offering 8-zone RGB customization that allows you to create dazzling lighting effects that match your gaming aesthetic. The lighting presets and customization options are visually impressive and add an extra layer of immersion to gaming sessions. The keypress experience is decent, with membrane switches that provide a responsive feel. It's quieter than mechanical switches, which can be a plus for those who want to game without a noisy distraction. The dedicated media controls are handy for adjusting volume and playback without interrupting the gaming experience. However, there are a couple of areas where the Apex 3 TKL could see improvement. First, the keycaps feel somewhat basic and may not provide the premium tactile experience that some gamers seek. Additionally, while the RGB customization is visually appealing, the software interface for customization could be more user-friendly.
reviews.author: TT

reviews.title: Solid Keyboard For Pricepoint
reviews.comment: Have purchased two of these, fairly quiet keys that still deliver decent tactile feedback. Have had some intermittent problems where the number five is non-responsive (after more than 18 months of daily use). I’ve had other keyboards where the LED’s introduce noise into a mic used close to the keyboard, those issues are completely non-existent here. Would buy again, solid keyboard at the price point.

reviews.title: Pretty Lights
reviews.comment: My go to brand for gaming.  It's consistently good, has a solid feel, not loud clicky as I prefer that.  I tend to go a few years before changing out but they still work on my old rigs.  Paint wears out on the WSAD and spacebar where I rest my fingers but that's 1000's of hours of playing.  I usually strip the paint on those keys which lets the light through as they are opaque.  No compatible with Aura but works with other solutions like Signal.
